terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the bookings here, and try your constructors from main.

tasks.title: Give Booking a constructor
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, inside the class `Booking`, write three fields: a `String` called `passenger`, an `int` called `seats` and an `int` called `hour`. Then write a constructor `Booking(String passenger, int seats, int hour)` that gives each field the value of the parameter with its name.

Check makes bookings of its own with `new Booking(...)`, two at once included, and reads every field of each.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about constructors and the word `this`.
Write the three fields under the `// Task 1` comment.
Write the constructor: its name is the class's name, with nothing in front of it.
Take the `//` off the first two lines in `main` and run the file.
hints: A constructor looks like a method with the class's name and no type in front, not even `void`. With `void` in front it is a method, and `new` never runs it.
Inside the constructor, `passenger` alone means the parameter. `this.passenger` means the field of the booking being made.

tasks.title: Add a constructor for one seat
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a second constructor, `Booking(String passenger, int hour)`, for a booking of one seat. The constructor of Task 1 stays as it is. It builds on Task 1.

Check makes bookings with both constructors and reads every field of each.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about a second constructor.
Write its first line: the same name, with the two parameters the task gives.
Give every field a value: one of them is not among its parameters.
Take the `//` off the lines for the single booking in `main` and run the file.
hints: A class can have several constructors, as long as their parameters differ. `new` picks the one whose parameters fit.
A field this constructor does not set keeps what Java gives it, 0 for a number. One seat has to be set on purpose.
Either set the three fields yourself, or hand the work to the first constructor in one line: `this(passenger, 1, hour);`.

tasks.title: Count how often a booking moves
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, add a field `int moves`, which no constructor sets, and a `void` method `moveTo(int hour)` that gives the booking the new hour and adds one to `moves`. It builds on Task 1.

Check makes bookings of its own, reads `moves` before any move, moves the bookings, and reads `hour` and `moves` of each.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about what Java gives a field that nobody sets.
Write the field without a value.
Write `moveTo`: it changes two fields of the booking it is called on.
Take the `//` off the last lines in `main` and run the file.
hints: A number field nobody sets starts at 0, so a new booking has no moves without any line of yours.
The parameter is called `hour`, like the field, so the field needs `this.` in front. `int moves = 0;` inside the method would make a new variable, not change the field.
